knowledge.content: Task constraint: Only modify /app/user.cpp - do not modify any other files in the system
System has two libstdc++ versions: Debug at /usr/local/gcc-custom-debug/ (no optimizations), Release at /usr/local/gcc-custom-release/ (with optimizations). Modified in-house compiler.
Compiler libstdc++ source code location: /build/ directory
Requirement: No memory leaks detected by Valgrind
Problem: Program crashes in RELEASE mode but works in DEBUG mode

main.cpp implements CustomHeapManager class that allocates a 10MB buffer and provides custom allocate/deallocate methods. Global operator new/new[]/delete/delete[] are overridden to use g_custom_heap when it's active.

Application lifecycle: init() calls user_init() then creates g_custom_heap, run() calls user_main() then does Monte Carlo π estimation, shutdown() destroys g_custom_heap and calls user_cleanup(). Note: ~Application() destructor also calls shutdown().
user.cpp currently contains three empty functions: user_init(), user_cleanup(), and user_main(). Any fix must be implemented in these functions.
CustomHeapManager::deallocate() does nothing except check if ptr and heap_memory are valid - it's a simple bump allocator that doesn't actually free memory, only allocates linearly.
Critical: g_custom_heap is created at line 149 in Application::init() using placement new on malloc'd memory. It's destroyed in shutdown() by manually calling destructor then freeing the memory.
